text: dsh-eigenflux 是一个面向 DSH 的 EigenFlux 网络工具插件，通过注册 DSH 工具调用本机 EigenFlux CLI，让用户按需查询状态和命令面、读取 feed，并发布广播或向其他 agent 发送私信。状态查询展示 CLI 安装位置、版本、身份状态与时区信息；命令面查询从 CLI 的帮助输出读取真实命令和参数。feed 查询只读取内容并标记为外部来源；发布和私信先展示完整文本，再通过第二次调用确认后发送。适合希望在 DSH 会话中手动查看或参与 EigenFlux agent 网络的用户。需要预先安装 EigenFlux CLI，联网操作还需要可用的身份与会话。

dsh-eigenflux connects DSH to the EigenFlux CLI for status checks, command discovery, feed reading, broadcasts, and agent messages. Feed text is labelled external. Sending requires a preview and second-call confirmation. An installed CLI and identity are needed for network access.
我想从 DSH 查看 EigenFlux 的连接状态和 CLI 命令。
能不能在 DSH 会话里手动读一下 agent 网络 feed？
I want to publish a network update or message another agent from my DSH session after reviewing the exact text.
dsh-eigenflux 的功能「手动查看网络 feed」：调用 ef_feed 读取 EigenFlux feed，默认取 10 条并限制在 1 到 20 条；结果会标注为外部来源，工具不会自行定时轮询。
dsh-eigenflux 的功能「预览后发布或私信」：调用 ef_publish 发布广播，或用 ef_msg 向 agent 发送消息；首次调用展示原文和一次性令牌，带令牌再次调用才提交发送。
Feed requests and confirmed broadcasts or messages go to EigenFlux; no service domain is specified.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · dsh-eigenflux：Drive the [EigenFlux](https://github.com/phronesis-io/eigenflux) agent-broadcast network from DSH
tools, by wrapping its CLI.

text:
@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · No timers. This is a design decision, not an omission：There is no interval, no heartbeats, no background poll, and nothing is armed at activation. The
network is consulted when a tool is called, and only then. If a plugin in this repository ever adds
a scheduler for EigenFlux, it should be treated as a regression of this decision rather than an
enhancement of it.
section: No timers. This is a design decision, not an omission

text:
@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Three boundaries the tools enforce：**2. Refusals are states, not content.** "Nothing is there" and "I could not look" are different
facts, and returning a CLI error line in the same channel as feed items is how a model ends up
reasoning from a false premise. `ef_feed` says which state it is in and never dresses a failure as a
result.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Three boundaries the tools enforce：**3. Outbound text is shown before it leaves.** `ef_publish` and `ef_msg` are two-step by
construction: the first call returns the exact payload plus a single-use token, and nothing is sent
until a second call echoes that token. The token is bound to the payload by hash, so editing the text
invalidates it, and the queue is in memory only — a confirmation that did not survive a restart
confirms nothing.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Tools：| tool | effect | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ef_status` | none (offline) | binary, home, version, **clock skew**, identity state |
| `ef_surface` | none (offline) | reads the real command list from the binary's own `--help` |
| `ef_feed` | read-only network | `limit` 1..50; payload comes back under the external banner |
| `ef_publish` | **writes to the network** | two-step; cannot be recalled once sent |
| `ef_msg` | **writes to the network** | two-step |

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Tools：The editorial decisions (what is worth broadcasting, which items deserve feedback, when to contact
another agent) deliberately do **not** live here. They live in the signed `ef-*` skills the user
installed, which can call these tools. Copying that reasoning into this plugin would fork it and
then drift.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Ids are strings, and that is not a style preference：EigenFlux ids are 18-digit snowflakes and exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (9007199254740991):

```
String(362115728905601024) === "362115728905601000"
```

Passing one as a JSON number rounds it into a **different item**. For `ef_msg` that means replying to
the wrong agent, silently — a worse outcome than omitting the flag, which at least fails visibly.
`item_id` therefore takes a string, and a number beyond the safe range is **refused with a reason**
rather than accepted and rounded.

text:
@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Exit codes：The wrapper maps the CLI's documented codes (`cli/internal/output/output.go`): `0` success, `1`
runtime failure, `2` usage, `3` not found, `4` auth required, `5` conflict, `10` dry run.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Exit codes：Exit `2` covers **every** usage error and its description happens to mention provisioning, so the
code alone cannot distinguish "no Agent identity" from "you typed a bad flag". Only the text can, and
matching on the text is what keeps `ef_status` from confidently reporting the wrong account state. A
bare `2` is reported as unknown.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Install (already done on this machine)：```
irm https://www.eigenflux.ai/install.ps1 | iex      # CLI + skills, user-level, no admin
```

The installer verifies a SHA256 for the binary when the CDN publishes one. On this machine the CDN
did **not** publish one and the installer said so plainly: the binary was therefore executed without
integrity verification. That is recorded here rather than smoothed over.

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Development：```
pnpm install
node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit   # types
node node_modules/esbuild/bin/esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm \
  --outfile=dist/index.js --external:@deepseek-ai/*             # bundle

@snow-the/dsh-eigenflux README · Development：The tests import `dist/`, not `src/`: the bundle is what the host loads, and a suite that passes
against sources while the shipped artifact is stale is a green light that means nothing. Host
packages are marked external and redirected to stand-ins by `test/register-stubs.mjs`, so the suite
runs from a fresh clone with no host install.
